endpoints.name: add address
endpoints.description:
This endpoint adds a new address for the user.
        
    It receives address details
    It saves the new address
    It can set it as default
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a user adds a shipping or billing address.

endpoints.name: update address
endpoints.description:
This endpoint updates an existing address.
        
    It modifies the selected address details
    It saves the changes
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a user edits an address.

endpoints.name: delete address
endpoints.description:
This endpoint deletes an address.
        
    It finds the address by ID
    It removes it
    It returns success
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a user removes an address.

endpoints.name: get all addresses
endpoints.description:
This endpoint gets all saved addresses of the logged-in user.
        
    It returns the user’s address list
    It can show the default and other addresses
    Simple meaning: this API is used to view the user’s saved addresses.

endpoints.name: add brand
endpoints.description: Creates a new brand under a specific sub-category. A brand represents a company or product line like "Apple", "Samsung", "Sony", etc. Each brand must belong to a sub-category and category, have a unique name, and include a logo image. The system automatically generates a slug and verifies that the sub-category exists under the correct parent category before creating the brand.

endpoints.name: get brand
endpoints.description:
This endpoint gets one specific brand from the database.
        
    You can search by brand id, name, or slug
    It returns the matching brand if it exists
    If the brand is not found, it returns an error
    In simple words: this API is used when you want to view one brand only, such as a single brand by its name or unique ID.

endpoints.name: update brand
endpoints.description: Updates an existing brand's name or logo image. When the name changes, the slug is automatically regenerated. The new logo replaces the old one on cloud storage. The brand maintains its relationship with both its category and sub-category.

endpoints.name: delete brand
endpoints.description: Removes a brand completely from the system. This deletes the brand logo and its folder from cloud storage. Products under this brand may become orphaned if not handled separately, so consider your data structure before deletion.

endpoints.name: list related Brands
endpoints.description:
This endpoint gets all brands that belong to a specific category or sub-category.
          
    You can filter by category
    You can also filter by subCategory
    It returns the brands connected to that category or sub-category
    In simple words: this API is used when you want to show brands that are related to a selected category or sub-category, such as “all brands under Men’s Shoes”.
endpoints.exampleName: Get brand related to sub-category or category or both

endpoints.name: list all brands
endpoints.description:
This endpoint is used to get a list of all brands.
          
    It gives you extra features through ApiFeatures, so you can:
          
    paginate the results
    filter brands by conditions
    search brands by keyword
    sort brands by name or other fields
    In the easiest way:
          
    pagination() → split results into pages
    filter() → show only matching brands
    search() → find brands by text
    sort() → order the list
    Example requests:
          
    GET /brands?page=1&limit=10 → first page, 10 brands
    GET /brands?search=apple → find brands with “apple”
    GET /brands?sort=-name → sort from Z to A
    GET /brands?name=Apple → show only Apple brand
    The response includes:
          
    total: total number of matching brands
    page: current page
    data: the list of brands
    This makes the API easier to use in dashboards, frontend pages, and product filters.

endpoints.name: add to cart
endpoints.description:
This endpoint adds a product to the cart.
        
    It checks the product and user
    It adds the item to the cart
    It may update quantity if already exists
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a user adds an item to the cart.

bodyJson.message: Product has been added to cart

endpoints.name: remove from cart
endpoints.description:
This endpoint removes a product from the cart.
        
    It finds the cart item
    It deletes it from the cart
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a user removes an item from the cart.

bodyJson.message: Product has been removed form cart

endpoints.name: update cart
endpoints.description:
This endpoint updates the cart item quantity.
        
    It changes the product quantity
    It saves the updated cart
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a user changes the number of items in the cart.

endpoints.name: get cart
endpoints.description:
This endpoint returns the current cart.
        
    It lists the products in the cart
    It may show total price or quantities
    Simple meaning: this API is used to view the user’s shopping cart.

endpoints.name: add category
endpoints.description: Creates a new main product category in the system. This is used to organize products into broad groups like "Electronics", "Clothing", "Books", etc. When you add a category, you need to provide a unique name and an image that represents the category. The system automatically creates a slug from the name and stores the image in cloud storage. Each category is identified by a unique ID and tracks which admin created it.

endpoints.name: get category
endpoints.description: This endpoint gets one specific category from the database. You can search by category id, name, or slug It returns the matching category if it exists If no search value is provided, it returns an error If the category is not found, it returns a “not found” error In simple words: this API is used when you want to view one category only, such as a single category by its unique ID or name.

endpoints.name: update category
endpoints.description: Allows you to modify an existing category's information. You can update the category name, the image, or both. When the name changes, the system automatically updates the slug as well. The old image is replaced with the new one on cloud storage. This is useful when you need to rename categories or refresh their visual appearance.

endpoints.name: delete category
endpoints.description: Removes a category completely from the system. This also removes the category image from cloud storage. It's important to note that deleting a category may leave sub-categories and products without a parent category, so you should consider your data relationships before performing this action.

endpoints.name: list categories
endpoints.description:
This endpoint is used to get a list of all categories.
            
    It uses ApiFeatures, so it supports:
            
    pagination
    filtering
    searching
    sorting
    This means you can:
            
    show categories in pages
    find a specific category by name or condition
    search category names
    sort the results by a field
    Examples:
            
    GET /categories?page=1&limit=10 → first page, 10 categories
    GET /categories?search=mobile → search by category name
    GET /categories?sort=-name → sort from Z to A
    GET /categories?name=Electronics → show only that category
    The response includes:
            
    total: total number of categories
    page: current page
    data: category list
    Simple meaning: this API is for showing many categories in a clean and organized way.

endpoints.name: add coupon
endpoints.description: Creates a new discount coupon code that can be applied during checkout. You need to provide a unique coupon code (like "SAVE50" or "SUMMER2025"), the validity period (start and end dates), the discount amount, and the type of discount (fixed amount or percentage). You can also specify which users are allowed to use this coupon. This is useful for promotions, seasonal sales, and customer incentives.

endpoints.name: get coupons
endpoints.description:
This endpoint gets all available coupons.
        
    It uses ApiFeatures, so it supports:
        
    pagination
    filtering
    sorting
    searching
    Examples:
        
    GET /coupons?page=1&limit=10
    GET /coupons?search=summer
    GET /coupons?sort=-discount
    Simple meaning: this API is used to show coupon offers to users.

endpoints.name: get specific coupon
endpoints.description:
This endpoint gets one specific coupon.
        
    It checks by coupon ID or code
    It returns the matching coupon
    If not found, it gives an error
    Simple meaning: this API is used to show one coupon’s details.

endpoints.name: update coupon
endpoints.description: Modifies an existing coupon's details. You can update the coupon code, validity dates, discount amount/type, eligible users, or enable/disable the coupon. All changes are logged in a change log for audit purposes, which tracks who made the change and what was modified. This allows you to manage coupons over time without deleting them.

endpoints.name: add order
endpoints.description:
This endpoint creates a new order.
          
    It takes order details
    It validates the items and user
    It saves the new order
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a customer places an order.

endpoints.name: cancel order
endpoints.description:
This endpoint cancels an existing order.
          
    It finds the order
    It changes status to canceled
    It returns success
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a user cancels their order.

endpoints.name: Get user's orders
endpoints.description:
This endpoint gets all orders for the logged-in user.
        
    It returns the user’s order history
    It may include statuses and totals
    Simple meaning: this API is used to view a user’s order history.

endpoints.name: Get order details
endpoints.description:
This endpoint gets the details of one order.
        
    It finds the specific order
    It returns complete order information
    Simple meaning: this API is used to view a single order’s full details.

endpoints.name: Deliver order
endpoints.description:
This endpoint marks an order as delivered.
        
    It finds the order
    It updates the delivery status
    Simple meaning: this API is used when the order is delivered to the customer.

endpoints.description: Creates a new product with complete details. This includes the product title, description, specifications (like size, color, features), pricing, discount information, stock quantity, and multiple product images. The system automatically calculates the final price after applying discounts, generates a slug from the title, and stores images in cloud storage. Each product is automatically linked to its brand, sub-category, and category.

endpoints.name: update product
endpoints.description: Updates any information about an existing product, including title, description, specifications, price, discount amount/type, stock quantity, and product badges (like "New", "Hot Sale", "Best Seller"). When the title changes, the slug is regenerated. When price or discount values change, the final price is automatically recalculated. You can update individual fields or multiple fields at once.

endpoints.name: list all products
endpoints.description:
his endpoint gets a list of all products.
          
    It uses ApiFeatures, so it supports:
          
    pagination
    filtering
    searching
    sorting
    Examples:
          
    GET /products?page=1&limit=10 → show page 1 with 10 products
    GET /products?search=laptop → search product names
    GET /products?categoryId=123 → show products in a category
    GET /products?sort=price → sort from low to high
    GET /products?sort=-price → sort from high to low
    Simple meaning: this API is used to show many products with smart filtering and page navigation.

endpoints.name: get product by id
endpoints.description:
This endpoint gets one product by its details.
        
    You can search by product ID or other unique values
    It returns the product data if found
    If the product does not exist, it returns an error
    Simple meaning: this API is used to view one product in detail.

endpoints.name: delete product
endpoints.description: Permanently removes a product from the system. All product images are deleted from cloud storage along with the entire product folder. This deletion doesn't affect existing orders that contain this product, but it may affect shopping carts and wishlists.

endpoints.name: add review
endpoints.description:
This endpoint adds a review for a product.
        
    It checks if the user already reviewed the product
    It checks if the user bought the product
    It saves the review
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a customer leaves feedback about a product.

endpoints.name: list reviews
endpoints.description:
This endpoint gets all reviews.
        
    It uses ApiFeatures when implemented in the list flow, so it can support:
        
    pagination
    filtering by product or user
    sorting by rating
    searching review text
    Examples:
        
    GET /reviews?page=1&limit=10
    GET /reviews?productId=123
    GET /reviews?sort=-reviewRating
    Simple meaning: this API is used to show customer reviews with filtering and sorting.

endpoints.name: accept or reject review
endpoints.description: Moderates a product review submitted by a customer. This endpoint allows an admin to either approve a review to make it publicly visible to other customers, or reject it if it violates guidelines or is inappropriate. Once you choose to approve or reject, that status is recorded. Approved reviews appear on the product page, while rejected reviews are hidden from public view.

endpoints.name: add sub category
endpoints.description: Creates a sub-category under a parent category to further organize products. For example, under "Electronics" you might have "Smartphones", "Laptops", "Cameras". Sub-categories must belong to an existing category and each sub-category needs a unique name and an image. The system automatically generates a slug and organizes images in a nested folder structure based on the parent category.

endpoints.name: get specific sub category
endpoints.description: This endpoint gets one specific sub-category from the database. You can search by sub-category id, name, or slug It returns the matching sub-category if it exists If the sub-category is not found, it returns an error In simple words: this API is used when you want to view one sub-category only, such as a single sub-category by its ID or name.

endpoints.name: update sub category
endpoints.description: Updates an existing sub-category's name, image, or both. Similar to category updates, the slug is automatically regenerated when the name changes, and the image is replaced on cloud storage. The sub-category maintains its relationship with the parent category.

endpoints.name: Delete sub category
endpoints.description: Permanently removes a sub-category from the system. When you delete a sub-category, all brands associated with that sub-category are automatically deleted as well (cascading deletion). The sub-category images are removed from cloud storage.

bodyJson.message: Sub category has been deleted successfully

endpoints.name: List sub categories
endpoints.description: This endpoint is used to get a list of all sub-categories. It also uses ApiFeatures, so it supports: pagination filtering searching sorting Examples: GET /sub-categories?page=1&limit=10 → page 1, 10 sub-categories GET /sub-categories?categoryId=123 → show sub-categories under a specific category GET /sub-categories?search=shoes → search sub-category names GET /sub-categories?sort=name → sort from A to Z The response includes: total: total number of matching sub-categories page: current page data: list of sub-categories Simple meaning: this API is for showing many sub-categories with search, filter, and page options.

endpoints.name: register
endpoints.description:
This endpoint creates a new user account.
      
    It receives username, email, password, and address details
    It validates the data
    It creates the user and default address
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a new user signs up.

endpoints.name: Update profile
endpoints.description:
This endpoint updates the logged-in user’s information.
        
    It can update password, email, username, phone, and other account fields
    It can also update the default address
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a user edits their profile.

endpoints.name: login
endpoints.description:
This endpoint logs a user in.
      
    It checks the email and password
    If correct, it returns a token
    This token is used in protected routes
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a user signs in.

endpoints.name: Delete user profile
endpoints.description:
This endpoint deletes the logged-in user account.
        
    It finds the user
    It removes the account from the database
    It returns success
    Simple meaning: this API is used when the user deletes their account.

bodyJson.message: User account has been deleted successfully

endpoints.name: Get user profile
endpoints.description:
This endpoint returns the current user’s profile.
        
    It gets the user information
    It also gets the default address
    It hides the password in the response
    Simple meaning: this API is used to fetch the logged-in user data.

endpoints.name: Forgot password copy
endpoints.description:
This endpoint starts the password reset flow.
        
    It checks if the email exists
    It creates an OTP token for password reset
    Simple meaning: this API is used when a user forgets their password.
endpoints.exampleName: First phase of forgotten password phases

bodyJson.message: Otp has been sent on you email ososmeedo@gmail.com successfully

endpoints.name: Verify OTP copy
endpoints.description:
This endpoint verifies the OTP sent to the user.
              
    It checks the OTP and token
    If correct, it returns a reset token
    Simple meaning: this API is used to confirm the identity of the user before resetting the password.
endpoints.exampleName: Second phase of forgotten password phases

endpoints.name: Reset password copy
endpoints.description:
This endpoint sets a new password.
              
    It receives the reset token and new password
    It validates the token
    It updates the password
    Simple meaning: this API is used to finish the password reset process.
endpoints.exampleName: Final phase of forgotten password phases
